newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Twenty-six killed in Somali fighting for airstrip.
newsitem.headline: Twenty-six killed in Somali fighting for airstrip.

text.p: Twenty-six people were killed and 48 wounded on Wednesday when forces of Somali faction leader Ali Hassan Osman Atto attacked and captured an airstrip from militiamen of his rival Hussein Aideed, witnesses said.
In north Mogadishu, militiamen loyal to faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohammed seized the main Islamic court prison, killing two militiamen and wounding one, and freed the prisoners, witnesses said.
The raid on the prison lasted about 15 minutes and followed recent friction between Ali Mahdi and the Islamic court.

Other witnesses said earlier on Wednesday Osman Atto's militiamen attacked Aideed's forces at Middle Shabelle airstrip, 50 km (30 miles) from Mogadishu, and seized it in an attack with eight "technical" four-wheel-drive battlewagons.

Abdi Osman, a man wounded in the fighting and taken to the Hassan Jiis Memorial Hospital in Mogadishu, said Atto's militiamen shot at anything in sight at the strip -- used mainly by suppliers of the mild stimulant qat from neighbouring Kenya.
Osman said an Indian pilot who had landed in his Cessna plane carrying qat was captured and his plane was hit. He said 26 people were killed and 48 were wounded including himself.

On Tuesday, 13 people were killed and up to 16 others wounded in an attack by unidentified gunmen in the Bar Ubah area inhabited by Hussein Aideed supporters south of Mogadishu. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack.
Witnesses said the gunmen sped up to the open-air Muna restaurant near the largest market in south Mogadishu and fired a rocket-propelled grenade into it and raked it with machinegunfire.

The fighting this week was the bloodiest flare up since Somali factions -- including Atto and Aideed -- agreed in Nairobi two weeks ago to end hostilities, remove roadblocks and pledged a continuation of dialogue for a peace process. The peace deal was brokered by Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi.

On Tuesday night, Abdullahi Mohamed, an Osman Atto supporter, was killed in an attack on his house in Mogadishu by unidentified assailants, witnesses said. It was not known whether the airstrip had anything to do with his killing.

South Mogadishu has been hit since September by a string of assassinations, attacks and counter-attacks which Somali experts say are part of a vendetta between groups over Mohamed Farah Aideed's death.
Since last month supporters of Aideed have killed more than 10 people who backed Atto, a rival south Mogadishu faction leader whose forces are widely blamed for killing Farah Aideed.
Aideed, like his father, was elected president of Somalia by supporters and heads a government. But it has not received much international recognition and is rejected by most other leaders.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow by rebels of late dictator president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
